(2009) }} '''Thomas Earl Robinson''' (born March 17, 1991) is an American-born naturalised Lebanese{{cite news |title=Thomas Robinson gets Lebanese passport, will play for NT in FIBA WC Qualifiers |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/thomas-robinson-gets-lebanese-passport-will-play-for-nt-in-fiba-wc-qualifiers/ |website=Sportando |date=December 6, 2021 |access-date=December 15, 2021 |last1=Carchia |first1=Emiliano }} professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Leones de Ponce (basketball)|Leones de Ponce]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]] (BSN). A consensus [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] at the [[University of Kansas]], Robinson was drafted fifth overall in the [[2012 NBA draft]] by the [[Sacramento Kings]]. ==High school career== Robinson grew up in Washington, DC, and attended [[Eastern High School (Washington, D.C.)|Eastern High School]], and [[Riverdale Baptist School|Riverdale Baptist]] before moving on to the [[Brewster Academy]] in [[Wolfeboro, New Hampshire]]. Robinson averaged 16 points, 13 rebounds and 5 blocks per game his senior year. Robinson was ranked as the No. 24 recruit by Scout.com, No. 31 by Rivals.com{{cite web|url=http://rivals.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/recruiting/player-Thomas-Robinson-83404 |title=Thomas Robinson - Yahoo! Sports |publisher=Rivals.yahoo.com |date=April 20, 2011 |access-date=November 9, 2012}} and No. 40 by ESPN.com as a high school senior.{{cite web|url=http://www.kuathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/robinson_thomas00.html|title=Thomas Robinson Profile - University of Kansas Official Athletic Site|publisher=Kuathletics.com|access-date=November 9, 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121022100952/http://www.kuathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/robinson_thomas00.html|archive-date=October 22, 2012}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2009}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Thomas Robinson | position = PF | hometown = Washington, DC | highschool =Brewster Academy | feet = 6 | inches = 8 | weight = 222 |40 = | commitdate = October 10, 2008 | scout stars = 5 | rivals stars = 4 | espn grade = 93 }} |} ==College career== [[File:20120128 Royce White defending of Iowa State against Thomas Robinson of the Kansas Jayhawks.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Robinson at Kansas.]] Robinson began his junior year and the 2011–2012 men's college basketball season as one of 50 candidates for the preseason [[John R. Wooden Award]].{{cite web|url=http://www.woodenaward.com/?p=1105|title=John R Wooden Award|access-date=September 26, 2016}} Along with senior teammate [[Tyshawn Taylor]], Robinson was expected to become one of the leaders for the Kansas team. On December 31, 2011, in a game against the [[University of North Dakota men's basketball|University of North Dakota]], Robinson scored 30 points and grabbed 21 rebounds. He was the first Kansas player to record a 30/20 performance since [[Wayne Hightower]] scored 36 points and grabbed 21 rebounds in a 1961 game against the [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|University of Missouri]].{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=313652305 |archive-url=http://web.archive.org/web/20150610203524/http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=313652305 |url-status=dead |archive-date= 2015-06-10|title=North Dakota vs. Kansas Jayhawks - Recap - December 31, 2011 - ESPN |publisher=ESPN |date=December 31, 2011 |access-date=November 9, 2012}} At the end of the Big 12 conference regular season, Robinson was second in the nation with 22 [[double-double|double doubles]] behind [[O.D. Anosike]] of [[Siena Saints men's basketball|Siena College]]. At that point, Robinson averaged 18 points and 11.9 rebounds. Prior to their game on January 22, 2011, against [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]], Kansas players, coaches and fans held a moment of silence in honor of Robinson, who had lost his grandmother, grandfather, and mother all within three weeks of one another. After the game, Kansas coach [[Bill Self]] said "For him to even be out there on the court was remarkable."{{cite news |title=Thomas Robinson's mother dies |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=6048355 |work=[[ESPN.com]] |date=January 22, 2011 |access-date=March 6, 2012}} On March 4, 2012, Robinson was named the [[Big 12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|2012 Big 12 Player of the Year]]. All-Big 12 awards are selected by the league's head coaches.{{cite news|url=http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/kan/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/2011-12/misc_non_event/12allbig12.pdf|title=2012 Phillips 66 All-Big 12 Men's Basketball Awards Announced|author=Big 12 Conference|publisher=Big 12 Conference|access-date=March 4, 2011|archive-date=September 28, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130928032518/http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/kan/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/2011-12/misc_non_event/12allbig12.pdf|url-status=dead}} On March 5, 2012, he was named the Associated Press Big 12 Player of the Year.{{cite web|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2012/basketball/ncaa/wires/03/05/2060.ap.bkc.all.big.12.team.1st.ld.writethru.0957|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140327203902/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2012/basketball/ncaa/wires/03/05/2060.ap.bkc.all.big.12.team.1st.ld.writethru.0957/|url-status=dead|archive-date=March Wooden Award]] Finalist{{cite web | title = Kansas' Thomas Robinson Named Naismith Men's College Basketball Player of the Year Finalist | url = http://www.kuathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/031912aaa.html | publisher = Kansas Athletics Official Website | date = March 19, 2012 | access-date = March 19, 2012 }} (2012) *[[Naismith College Player of the Year]] Finalist (2012) ==Professional career== ===Sacramento Kings (2012–2013)=== On June 28, 2012, Robinson was drafted fifth overall in the [[2012 NBA draft]] by the [[Sacramento Kings]]. On November 7, 2012, in the fourth quarter of a game against the [[Detroit Pistons]], Robinson hit [[Jonas Jerebko]] in the throat with an elbow, and was ejected from the game.{{cite web | last=Glover | first=Ben | url=https://www.si.com/nba/point-forward/2012/11/08/thomas-robinson-ejected-jonas-jerebko-pistons-kings | title=Kings' Robinson ejected for vicious elbow to throat of Pistons' Jerebko | work=Sports Illustrated | date=November 8, 2012 | access-date=September 21, 2016}} The following day, he was suspended for two games.{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/2012/news/11/08/thomas-robinson-kings-suspended/ | title=Kings rookie Robinson suspended for throwing elbow | work=NBA.com | date=November 8, 2012 | access-date=September 21, 2016}} ===Houston Rockets (2013)=== On February 21, 2013, Robinson was traded, along with [[Francisco García (basketball)|Francisco García]] and [[Tyler Honeycutt]], to the [[Houston Rockets]] in exchange for [[Patrick Patterson (basketball)|Patrick Patterson]], [[Toney Douglas]], [[Cole Aldrich]] and cash considerations.{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-acquire-robinson-garcia-and-honeycutt | title=Rockets Acquire Robinson, Garcia and Honeycutt | work=NBA.com | date=February 21, 2013 | access-date=September 21, 2016}}{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-complete-multiplayer-trade | title=KINGS COMPLETE MULTIPLAYER TRADE | work=NBA.com | date=February 21, 2013 | access-date=September 21, 2016}} Robinson was given up on by the Kings due to the emergence of [[DeMarcus Cousins]] as well as the Kings' struggles to find playing time for Robinson.{{Cite magazine|last=Golliver|first=Ben|title=Kings trade Thomas Robinson to Rockets in multi-player deal|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2013/02/21/thomas-robinson-trade-kings-rockets|access-date=July 28, 2021|magazine=Sports Illustrated|date=February 20, 2013 |language=en-us}} ===Portland Trail Blazers (2013–2015)=== On July 10, 2013, Robinson was traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in exchange for the rights to [[Kostas Papanikolaou]] and [[Marko Todorović (basketball)|Marko Todorović]], as well as two future second-round picks.{{cite web | url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=13700 | title=Rockets trade Thomas Robinson to Trail Blazers | work=InsideHoops.com | date=July 10, 2013 | access-date=September 21, 2016}}{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-acquire-papanikolaou-todorovic-and-two-future-2nd-round-picks | title=Rockets Acquire Papanikolaou, Todorovic and Two Future 2nd Round Picks | work=NBA.com | date=July 10, 2013 | access-date=September 21, 2016}} On February 23, 2014, Robinson recorded 14 points and a career-high 18 rebounds in a 108–97 win over the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20140223/MINPOR/gameinfo.html|title=Notebook: Trail Blazers 108, Timberwolves 97|work=NBA.com|date=February 23, 2014|access-date=February 23, 2014}} In 2013–14, he averaged 4.8 points and 4.4 rebounds in 70 games.{{Cite web |title=Thomas Robinson Career Stats - NBA |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/stats/_/id/6618/thomas-robinson |access-date=February 21, 2024 |website=ESPN |language=en}} The 2014–15 season saw Robinson consigned to the bench, buried on the depth chart by the team's off-season addition of former All-Star big man [[Chris Kaman]]. Robinson's first real opportunity of the season came with the injury of starting center [[Robin Lopez]], who fractured his right hand on December 15 in a win over the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite web|last=Freeman|first=Joe|url=http://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/index.ssf/2014/12/robin_lopez_breaks_right_hand_forcing_trail_blazer.html|title=Robin Lopez fractures right hand, forcing Trail Blazers to think about playing without missing link|work=OregonLive.com|date=December 15, 2014|access-date=March 29, 2016}} Robinson made his first NBA start in the team's next game, a December 17 home contest against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], racking up 15 points and 16 rebounds to help the Trail Blazers win 104–97. He became the third Blazers player to put up at least 15 points and 15 rebounds in his first start; the other two being [[Bill Walton]] and [[Maurice Lucas]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141217/MILPOR/gameinfo.html|title=Aldridge, Trail Blazers rally to beat Bucks 104-97|work=NBA.com|date=December 17, 2016|access-date=March 29, 2016}} In subsequent games, Robinson was paired with Kaman off the bench, playing solid reserve minutes as power forward behind [[LaMarcus Aldridge]].{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/r/robinth01/gamelog/2015/|title=Thomas Robinson 2014-15 Game Log|work=Basketbal-Reference.com|access-date=March 29, 2016}} ===Philadelphia 76ers (2015)=== On February 19, 2015, Robinson was traded, along with [[Will Barton]], [[Víctor Claver]] and a lottery-protected 2016 first-round pick, to the [[Denver Nuggets]] in exchange for [[Arron Afflalo]] and [[Alonzo Gee]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-acquire-barton-claver-robinson-and-protected-first-round-pick-portland|title=Nuggets Acquire Barton, Claver, Robinson and Protected First Round Pick From Portland - Denver Nuggets|website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=September 26, 2016}} Three days later, he was waived by the Nuggets before playing in a game for them.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-waive-claver-and-robinson|title=Nuggets Waive Claver and Robinson - Denver Nuggets|website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=September 26, 2016}} On February 24, 2015, Robinson was claimed off waivers by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/150224-robinson-claimed|title=Sixers Claim Thomas Robinson - Philadelphia 76ers|website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=September 26, 2016}} The next day, he made his debut for the 76ers, recording seven points and six rebounds in a 104–88 loss to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150225/PHIMIL/gameinfo.html|title=76ers at Bucks|website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=September 26, 2016}} ===Brooklyn Nets (2015–2016)=== On July 9, 2015, Robinson signed with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-re-sign-brook-lopez-and-thaddeus-young |title=Player Signing Press Conference |work=NBA.com |date=July 9, 2015 |access-date=July 10, 2015 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150711235023/http://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-re-sign-brook-lopez-and-thaddeus-young |archive-date=July 11, 2015 }} He made his debut for the Nets in the team's season opener against the [[Chicago Bulls]] on October 28, recording four points and five rebounds off the bench in a 115–100 loss.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/CHIBKN/gameinfo.html|title=Bulls beat Nets 115-100 for 2-0 start|work=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2015|access-date=October 28, 2015}} On March 5, 2016, he had a season-best game with 18 points and 17 rebounds in 40 minutes as a starter in a 132–118 loss to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. On March 29, he made just his second start of the season and again scored 18 points, this time in a loss to [[Orlando Magic]].{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/r/robinth01/gamelog/2016/|title=Thomas Robinson 2015-16 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=March 29, 2016}} On April 3, he recorded his fourth straight double-double with 11 points and 15 rebounds in a 106–87 loss to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160403/NOPBKN/gameinfo.html|title=Frazier has 19 points, 13 assists, Pelicans top Nets 106-87|work=NBA.com|date=April 3, 2016|access-date=April 3, 2016}} ===Los Angeles Lakers (2016–2017)=== On September 21, 2016, Robinson signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/160921-thomas-robinson|title=Lakers Sign Thomas Robinson|work=NBA.com|date=September 21, 2016|access-date=September 21, 2016}} On March 21, 2017, Robinson scored a season-high 16 points in a 133–109 loss to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. He tied that mark on April 1, 2017, recording 16 points and nine rebounds in another loss to the Clippers. A day later, Robinson recorded his first double-double of the season with 12 points and 10 rebounds in a 108–103 win over the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/r/robinth01/gamelog/2017/|title=Thomas Robinson 2016-17 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|date=April 2, 2017}} ===Khimki (2017–2018)=== On
